chapter: George Lewis and the 1946 Jazz Foundation concert
title: Joining the local and playing for the Shriners
summary: Williams says the band was put into the white local after that 1946 show at no cost, and that later he played a Shriners dance with Lars Edegran, Clive Wilson, Paul Barbarin and Jesse Charles.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: You weren't in the local before that?

No, we was on union. So this fellow, Kennedy, he told me, he said, yeah, he said, y'all got a damn nice set up here. And he said, it's pitiful to be a left-wing monkey ranch. He said, tonight we just got to have y'all on that show. And them guys worked all that day hard. You know, the day before that, going back and forth with Houston. And then they got to set up and give us a couple. Jim Crow, Slow Drag, George Lewis, me, and Lawrence Morell. It didn't cost us a nickel. They put us in there and we were in there ever since.
At Scoop County, they got on.

Yeah. And that, we went on from there and there. Never did catch us in no violation or nothing. You know what I mean? We went along. And we did, we did pretty good. Because I had a lot of connections from one job to the other. That's how I'm going to work through right now. I got a big job coming up, I'm going to let you know, because I want you and him to come. I wanted to get you out to dance. I had you boys up there at the Union Hall up there that night. And I played for the shrines from all over the world it was. I played their dance up there. And I had these two boys on trumpet and I had Leroy and I had the other little fella on piano.
Yeah, you know a little piano player played a lot of the time with Barker. He lives where you live at, don't he?
Yeah. And Sheik. Sheik told me about that I think, or they told me about it.
They all had them up there.
Oh yeah, yeah, they did tell me about that.
